findings.view: synthetic-earth.png and hover-debris-orbit.png (over the Earth disc from (665,322) to (637,400); off the disc x 400-600, y 400-720); synthetic-8-patches-earth.png (x 590-670, y 320-420 and the two pairs below); scene-synthetic.png / synthetic-chain.png (x 495-640, y 365-618)
findings.defect: Previous A1 is still visible where it was reported. Two planned patches that converge into the entry point run 1-3 px apart over the Earth disc. Their mauve and salmon dashes interleave into a jagged staircase, read at a glance as a broken or aliased line. Below the disc the same two legs become two 'railway tracks': pairs of dashed lines 3-8 px apart in two close, muted hues (mauve and salmon), with unrelated dash phases. At the overview they look like three nearly parallel dashed strands between the Earth and Enter Moon.
findings.realReference: KSP / KSP 2 / Juno: a plan is drawn as one chain. Past a later node only the newest plan continues, and two strokes never share a pixel corridor. Where two legs genuinely run side by side they have clearly distinct hues and a gap of at least one line width.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/scene.ts suppressCoincident (lines 1287-1298) hides a later segment only if it lies within COINCIDENT_PX = 3 (constants.ts line 80) of drawn cells 'for most of its on-screen length'. Where two legs converge, from 8 px to 0 px across the disc, each long segment is partly inside and partly outside that corridor, so both stay drawn. Each line has its own dash phase.
findings.fixDirection: Make the coincidence test per sub-span, not per segment: split at the point where the distance crosses about 1.5 line widths and hide only the covered part. Alternatively, when the plan after node N supersedes the earlier plan's continuation, do not draw that continuation at all. Where two legs stay parallel, give them clearly distinct hues (planned-1 orange, planned-2 magenta) at full saturation. Add a browser pixel check over the Earth disc in synthetic-earth.png that no two dash colours alternate within a 4 px corridor.

findings.realReference: In shipped maps a plate-less body name has a dark halo or outline, or it is placed off the lines. A trajectory never passes through the letters of a planet name.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/controller.ts lines 1311-1315 set labelStyle 'body' (no plate). labels.ts declutter treats line coverage as a cost, not a hard reject, so the cheapest free slot beside the Moon icon can lie on the dashed patch, and with no plate nothing masks it.
findings.fixDirection: Give body names a 2-3 px dark text halo (the same casing colour as the lines), or reject body-name candidates that cross a trajectory when another free candidate exists. Add a unit test: no body-name rectangle intersects a drawn current or planned polyline in the synthetic Moon view.

findings.view: accept-panel.png (cyan Ap marker (535,431), label 'Ap 200.0 km' x 447-523, y 443-472; yellow Ap marker (555,458), label 'Ap 371.5 km' x 566-640, y 417-447)
findings.defect: The two apoapsis labels are now tinted by patch and have short leaders, so a careful reader pairs them correctly. The layout is still crossed, though: each label sits level with the other marker, the cyan label beside the yellow marker and the yellow label beside the cyan one. The leaders cross the line between the markers. At a glance the rows still pair the wrong value with the wrong marker.
findings.realReference: KSP prints each apsis value on the outer side of its own orbit. Two nearby markers of different patches get labels on opposite sides of the trajectory pair, never crossed.
findings.likelyCause: labels.ts declutter: the foreign-icon penalty compares distance to the nearest icon, but the diagonal candidates (cases 4-7) put the plate level with the neighbour. The first label placed takes the other's natural side.
findings.fixDirection: In declutter, add a crossing check: reject or heavily penalise a candidate whose leader segment crosses the leader or anchor line of an already-placed label. Prefer, for markers of different patches within about 40 px, the outer side of each one's own patch.

findings.view: synthetic-moon.png and hover-impact-details.png (Impact plate x 403-625, y 314-346; the dashed planned patch enters under it at about (545,312) and leaves at (580,348)); dpr2-synthetic-moon.png (same, about x 1206-1872, y 941-1037); real-hud-lowOrbit-node-4k.png ('Central Pacific' plate over its own ring, about x 1350-1630, y 1440-1495)
findings.defect: Labels still sit on lines and mask them. The Impact plate hides about 50 px of the dashed planned patch where it bends round the Moon, which is the most important part of the plan. The 'Central Pacific' plate covers a stretch of its own recovery ring. Empty black space is free 30-60 px away in both cases.
findings.realReference: Shipped maps place a marker label off the trajectory, on the outer side. A plate is the fallback, never the first choice near the stroke it labels.
findings.likelyCause: labels.ts: line coverage is only one term of the cost, and candidates are searched in rank order with an early exit once 'best <= rank'. A cheap near candidate over a line therefore wins before a far ring candidate on empty space is scored. Zone rings carry a low LineGrid weight.
findings.fixDirection: Weight trajectory coverage high enough that any line-free candidate on the outer ring beats a line-covering near one. Remove the early exit when the best candidate so far covers a trajectory. Give a zone ring's own label a cost for covering its ring.

findings.view: scene-synthetic-intercept.png and synthetic-chain-intercept.png (cluster x 400-500, y 575-645: Exit Moon (404,575), encounter Moon ring (446,609), Node 1 (461,611) with '+2', Enter Moon (495,618), '+1' at (488,632), Ap (476,643))
findings.defect: At the at-intercept overview the encounter region is a knot: six icons, two count badges, four plated labels and three leaders in about 130 x 60 px. The '+1' badge is equally near the Enter Moon icon and the Ap icon, so it is unclear what it counts. The encounter Moon is a 5 px grey ring under the Node 1 icon with no name. findings.realReference: KSP 2 / Juno: badges overlap the corner of their icon. At a zoom where an encounter becomes a knot, the encounter is one marker ('Moon encounter') whose tooltip or zoom shows the detail.
findings.likelyCause: Clustering (CLUSTER_PX) merges by screen distance, but the badge position is computed from the owner's radius without checking that it is nearer its owner than any other icon. The encounter ghost body is not a cluster owner.
findings.fixDirection: Place the badge on the owner's corner that is farthest from other icons and assert that it is nearer its owner than any foreign icon. At this zoom let the encounter ghost own the cluster and carry one 'Moon encounter' label, with the members in the tooltip.

findings.view: accept-node-added.png -> accept-prograde-drag.png (pad label x 742-998, y 446-460 -> x 598-855, y 450-464)
findings.defect: Between two consecutive frames of a prograde drag (0 -> 10 m/s) the launch-site label jumps 144 px from the right of its icon to below-left of it, although its anchor did not move. During a drag labels will flicker between slots.
findings.realReference: Shipped map labels keep their slot while it stays free (hysteresis) and move only when blocked, with a short fade.
findings.likelyCause: labels.ts declutter is stateless: each frame it rescores all candidates, and a small change in the planned line's coverage cost flips the cheapest slot. There is no hysteresis.
findings.fixDirection: Remember each label's last slot by id and give it a bonus of one or two rank units while it stays free. Add a browser check over a 10-step handle drag that no label of an unmoved anchor changes slot.
